1.heading: Purpose, sources, investigation, and Theophilus
1.note: Luke says many have written accounts; having traced everything accurately, he writes in order to Theophilus so he may know the certainty

1.heading: John announced to Zechariah
1.note: Old and childless, Zacharias is told by Gabriel at the incense altar of a son, John; for doubting he is silenced, and Elizabeth conceives

1.heading: Jesus announced to Mary
1.note: Gabriel tells Mary, pledged to Joseph, she will bear a son named Jesus; she asks how, then says 'let it be done to me'.

1.heading: Mary and Elizabeth; the Magnificat
1.note: Mary hurries to Elizabeth, and the baby leaps in Elizabeth's womb; Mary sings of the mighty, the lowly and the hungry

1.heading: John born and named
1.note: Elizabeth bears a son; relatives would name him Zacharias, but she says John, and Zacharias writes the same on a tablet and speaks again

1.heading: Zechariah's Benedictus and John's growth
1.note: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Zacharias blesses God for salvation in David's house and tells the child he will go before the Lord

2.heading: Registration, journey, birth, and manger
2.note: A decree sends all to enroll in their cities; Joseph and Mary go to Bethlehem, where she lays her firstborn in a feeding trough

2.heading: Shepherds receive and spread the angelic announcement
2.note: Shepherds watching sheep at night see an angel and a heavenly army; they find the baby in a feeding trough and tell others

2.heading: Circumcision, purification, Simeon, and Anna
2.note: He is named Jesus at eight days; Simeon takes the child in his arms and Anna speaks of him; the family returns to Nazareth

2.heading: The twelve-year-old Jesus in his Father's house
2.note: Left behind at twelve, he is found after three days among the temple teachers; he says he must be in 'my Father's house'.

3.heading: Rulers named; God's word comes to John
3.note: Tiberius reigns; Pilate, Herod, Philip and Lysanias hold rule; Annas and Caiaphas are high priests when God's word comes to John in the wilderness

3.heading: Repentance and Isaiah's road for all flesh
3.note: John preaches the baptism of repentance around the Jordan, and Isaiah's words speak of valleys filled, mountains brought low, and all flesh seeing salvation

3.heading: Fruit in possessions, taxes, and military power
3.note: John calls the crowds 'offspring of vipers' and says share coats and food; tax collectors take no more than appointed; soldiers do not extort

3.heading: Stronger one, Spirit, fire, and John's imprisonment
3.note: People wonder if John is the Christ; he says a mightier one will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire; Herod imprisons John

3.heading: Jesus baptized, praying, and named Son
3.note: Jesus is baptized and praying; the sky opens, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice says 'my beloved Son'.

3.heading: Genealogy from Jesus back to Adam and God
3.note: Jesus is about thirty, son of Joseph as supposed; the list runs back through David, Abraham and Noah to Adam, 'the son of God'.

4.heading: Spirit-led testing in the wilderness
4.note: Fasting forty days, Jesus is tempted by the devil: stone to bread, all the kingdoms, the temple pinnacle; he answers 'It is written'.

4.heading: Return in the Spirit and synagogue teaching
4.note: Jesus returns to Galilee in the Spirit's power; news spreads, and he teaches in their synagogues, glorified by all

4.heading: Isaiah read and fulfilled today at Nazareth
4.note: At Nazareth on the Sabbath he reads Isaiah, sits, and says 'Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled'; they ask if he is Joseph's son

4.heading: Elijah–Elisha challenge and hometown rejection
4.note: He says no prophet is acceptable at home, citing a widow and Naaman; they lead him to a hill's brow, but he walks away

4.heading: Authority over an unclean spirit
4.note: A man with an unclean demon cries 'the Holy One of God'; Jesus says 'Be silent and come out of him', and it leaves

4.heading: Healings, solitude, and the must of kingdom mission
4.note: The fever leaves Simon's mother-in-law and she serves them; he heals the sick at sunset, then says other cities need 'the good news'.

5.heading: Teaching boat, great catch, and fisher disciples
5.note: He teaches from Simon's boat, then says let down nets; the catch fills two boats to sinking, and they leave everything and follow him

5.heading: A man cleansed by touch; Jesus withdraws to pray
5.note: A man with leprosy falls on his face; Jesus touches him, saying 'I want to', and the leprosy leaves; he then withdraws to pray

5.heading: Friends, roof, forgiveness, and a paralyzed man walking
5.note: Men lower a paralyzed man through the tiles; Jesus forgives his sins, then tells him to take up his cot and go home

5.heading: Levi called and a banquet with tax collectors
5.note: Jesus tells tax collector Levi 'Follow me'; Levi leaves everything, hosts a feast, and the Pharisees complain; Jesus says the sick need a physician

5.heading: Bridegroom, fasting, patches, and wineskins
5.note: Asked about fasting, he speaks of the bridegroom taken away, a new patch on an old garment, and new wine in old wineskins

6.heading: Grain, David, and Lord of the Sabbath
6.note: Pharisees object to disciples eating grain; Jesus recalls David eating the show bread and calls the Son of Man lord of the Sabbath

6.heading: A hand restored on the Sabbath
6.note: Watched by the scribes and Pharisees, Jesus has a man stretch out his withered hand, and it is restored; they are filled with rage

6.heading: Night prayer and the Twelve named apostles
6.note: After praying all night on the mountain, he chooses twelve disciples and names them apostles, including Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor

6.heading: Level place, healing, blessings, and woes
6.note: On a level place, crowds are healed; he blesses the poor, hungry, weeping and hated, then pronounces woes on the rich, full and laughing

6.heading: Enemy-love, mercy, generosity, and judgment
6.note: He says to love enemies, give to all who ask, be merciful, not judge, and remove the beam from one's own eye

6.heading: Trees, heart-speech, Lordship, and two foundations
6.note: A tree is known by its fruit; the mouth speaks from the heart; the one who hears and does builds on rock

7.heading: Centurion's mediated request and remarkable faith
7.note: Elders plead for a centurion's dying servant; the centurion sends friends saying 'say the word'; Jesus marvels, and the servant is found well

7.heading: Widow's only son raised at Nain
7.note: A widow's only son is carried out dead; Jesus says 'Don't cry', touches the coffin, and says 'arise'; the dead man sits up

7.heading: John asks; Jesus answers with deeds
7.note: John's two disciples ask if Jesus is the one coming; he cures many and tells them: the blind see, the dead are raised

7.heading: Jesus interprets John and this generation
7.note: Jesus asks what the crowds went to see, calls John 'much more than a prophet', and compares this generation to marketplace children

7.heading: Woman anoints Jesus; creditor parable and forgiveness
7.note: A sinful woman wets Jesus's feet with tears, wipes and anoints them; he tells of two debtors and says 'Your sins are forgiven'.

8.heading: Women and men in the traveling kingdom mission
8.note: On the road preaching with the twelve are healed women: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna and many others, who serve from their possessions

8.heading: Sower, soils, purpose, and persevering hearing
8.note: Seed falls on road, rock, thorns and good ground; Jesus says the seed is the word of God, and each ground a hearer

8.heading: Lamp, disclosure, measure, and hearing-doing family
8.note: A lit lamp goes on a stand; his mother and brothers, he says, are those who hear God's word and do it

8.heading: Storm stilled and fearful disciples
8.note: Jesus sleeps through a wind storm; woken, he rebukes wind and water, asks 'Where is your faith?', and they wonder who he is

8.heading: Legion expelled and a restored witness sent home
8.note: The man answers 'Legion'; the demons enter pigs that drown, the people ask Jesus to leave, and he sends the man home

8.heading: Jairus's daughter and the hemorrhaging woman
8.note: Jairus's daughter is dying; a woman touches his cloak and is healed on the way; he takes the dead girl's hand: 'Child, arise!'

9.heading: The Twelve sent; Herod asks who Jesus is
9.note: The twelve are sent to preach and heal, taking no staff, wallet, bread or money; Herod is perplexed and says 'I beheaded John'.

9.heading: Return and feeding of about five thousand
9.note: Crowds follow him to Bethsaida; 'You give them something to eat' — five loaves, two fish, about five thousand men, twelve baskets left

9.heading: Peter's confession, necessary suffering, and the cross
9.note: Peter says 'The Christ of God'; Jesus says he must suffer and be killed, and anyone following must take up his cross

9.heading: Transfiguration and Jerusalem ‘exodus’
9.note: His face changes, his clothes turn white, and Moses and Elijah talk with him; a voice from the cloud says 'Listen to him!'

9.heading: A boy freed; disciples misunderstand suffering and greatness
9.note: He heals a boy the disciples could not free; they argue about who is greatest, and he sets a little child by his side

9.heading: Face set to Jerusalem, Samaritan refusal, and costly following
9.note: A Samaritan village refuses him; James and John ask about fire from the sky; he rebukes them, then speaks to three people about following

10.heading: Seventy(-two) sent as workers and guests
10.note: Seventy others are sent two by two with no purse; they say 'Peace be to this house' and heal the sick

10.heading: Woes, representation, and return with joy
10.note: Woe to Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum; the seventy return with joy that demons obey; he says rejoice that their names are written in heaven

10.heading: Jesus rejoices in the Spirit and blesses witnesses
10.note: Jesus thanks the Father for revealing things to little children, then tells the disciples many prophets and kings wanted to see what they see

10.heading: Law, eternal life, and the merciful Samaritan
10.note: A lawyer asks about eternal life; Jesus tells of a robbed man passed by a priest and Levite, then cared for by a Samaritan

10.heading: Martha's welcome, anxious service, and Mary's listening
10.note: Martha, distracted with serving, asks him to tell Mary to help; he says 'one thing is needed' and Mary has chosen the good part

11.heading: A disciple asks; Jesus teaches the prayer
11.note: A disciple asks for teaching on prayer; he gives words from 'Our Father in heaven' to 'deliver us from the evil one'.

11.heading: Midnight persistence and the Father's Spirit gift
11.note: A friend asks at midnight for three loaves and gets them by persistence; Jesus says keep asking, and the Father gives the Holy Spirit

11.heading: Beelzebul accusation, divided rule, and stronger one
11.note: Some say he casts out demons by Beelzebul; he says a divided kingdom falls and that whoever is not with him is against him

11.heading: Returning spirit and hearing-kept blessing
11.note: A spirit returns with seven worse ones; a woman praises the womb that bore him; he blesses those who hear and keep God's word

11.heading: Jonah, southern queen, lamp, and eye
11.note: This generation gets only Jonah's sign; the Queen of the South and Nineveh's men will condemn it; the eye is the body's lamp

11.heading: Meal dispute and woes to Pharisees and lawyers
11.note: Over dinner he says Pharisees clean the cup's outside, then pronounces woes on Pharisees and lawyers; scribes and Pharisees lie in wait for him

12.heading: Hypocrisy exposed; fear, confession, and the Spirit
12.note: He warns of the Pharisees' yeast; not one of five sparrows is forgotten by God; the Holy Spirit will teach what to say

12.heading: Inheritance request, greed warning, and rich fool
12.note: Jesus declines to judge an inheritance, warns against covetousness, and tells of a rich man planning bigger barns whose soul is required that night

12.heading: Ravens, lilies, kingdom, little flock, and treasure
12.note: He tells his disciples not to be anxious, pointing to ravens and lilies, and to seek God's Kingdom and give to the needy

12.heading: Watchful servants and the returning master
12.note: Lamps burning, servants watch for their lord's return; he serves those found watching; the Son of Man comes in an hour you don't expect

12.heading: Faithful stewardship and proportionate accountability
12.note: Peter asks who the parable is for; the faithful steward is set over all; the servant who beats others is cut in two

12.heading: Fire, baptism, division, weather, and urgent settlement
12.note: He came to throw fire and bring division; crowds read clouds and wind but not this time; settle with an adversary on the way

13.heading: Pilate's victims, fallen tower, and universal repentance
13.note: Told of Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with sacrifices, he adds eighteen killed by a tower, and twice says 'unless you repent'.

13.heading: Barren fig tree granted cultivation and time
13.note: A man finds no fruit on his fig tree for three years and says cut it down; the vine dresser asks for another year

13.heading: A daughter of Abraham released on Sabbath
13.note: A woman bent over eighteen years stands straight after he lays hands on her; the ruler objects, and Jesus points to freeing an ox

13.heading: Mustard seed and yeast
13.note: God's Kingdom is like a mustard seed that becomes a large tree, and like yeast a woman hides in three measures of flour

13.heading: Narrow door, closed house, and surprising table
13.note: He says to strive to enter the narrow door; the master shuts it, saying 'I don't know you'; others come from four directions

13.heading: Herod the fox and Jesus's Jerusalem lament
13.note: Pharisees say Herod wants him dead; he calls Herod 'that fox', says he casts out demons today and tomorrow, and calls to Jerusalem

14.heading: Sabbath meal, watched healing, and silenced experts
14.note: Watched at a ruler's house, he asks if healing on the Sabbath is lawful; they are silent, and he heals a man with dropsy

14.heading: Lowest seat and honor received rather than seized
14.note: Seeing guests choose the best seats, he tells them to take the lowest place, so the host may say 'Friend, move up higher'.

14.heading: Invite those unable to repay
14.note: He tells his host to ask the poor, lame and blind, not friends or rich neighbors; the host will be repaid in the resurrection

14.heading: Great banquet, excuses, streets, and roads
14.note: Invited guests make excuses: a field, oxen, a wife; the angry master has the poor and lame brought in, then others from the highways

14.heading: Family, self, cross, and the cost of following
14.note: Turning to the crowds, he says whoever doesn't disregard family and his own life, or bear his own cross, 'can't be my disciple'.

14.heading: Tower, king, renunciation, and salt
14.note: A man counts the cost before building a tower, a king weighs ten thousand against twenty thousand; flat salt is thrown out

15.heading: Sinners draw near; religious critics complain about welcome
15.note: Tax collectors and sinners come close to hear him; the Pharisees and scribes murmur that he 'welcomes sinners, and eats with them'.

15.heading: Lost sheep, searching shepherd, and shared joy
15.note: A man leaves ninety-nine to find one lost sheep and calls friends to rejoice; Jesus says heaven has more joy over one repenting sinner

15.heading: Lost coin, searching woman, and angelic joy
15.note: A woman with ten coins loses one, lights a lamp and sweeps until she finds it, then calls her friends to rejoice

15.heading: Younger son demands, leaves, collapses, and returns
15.note: The younger son wastes his share abroad, feeds pigs, and resolves to go home and say 'Father, I have sinned'

15.heading: Father runs, restores, and begins the feast
15.note: While he is still far off his father runs and kisses him, then orders a robe, ring, sandals and the fattened calf

15.heading: Elder son refuses; father goes out and appeals
15.note: The elder son will not go in; his father comes out and begs him, and answers his complaint: 'all that is mine is yours'.

16.heading: Manager accused and acting before dismissal
16.note: Facing dismissal, a manager tells one debtor to write fifty for a hundred batos of oil, another eighty; the lord commends him

16.heading: Mammon, faithful stewardship, and two masters
16.note: He says the one faithful in little is faithful in much, and that no servant can serve two masters, 'God and Mammon'.

16.heading: Money-loving ridicule, heart, kingdom, law, and divorce
16.note: Scoffing Pharisees are told God knows their hearts; the law and prophets were until John; whoever divorces and marries another commits adultery

16.heading: Rich man and Lazarus in life and death
16.note: Beggar Lazarus lies sore-covered at a rich man's gate; both die, and Abraham tells the rich man in Hades a great gulf is fixed

16.heading: Moses, prophets, and refusal beyond a resurrection sign
16.note: He asks that Lazarus go to his brothers; Abraham says 'They have Moses and the prophets'; one rising from the dead would not persuade

17.heading: Stumbling, rebuke, repentance, and repeated forgiveness
17.note: Better a millstone around the neck than making a little one stumble; rebuke a sinning brother, and forgive him seven times a day

17.heading: Mustard-seed faith and servants without entitlement
17.note: The apostles ask 'Increase our faith'; he speaks of a sycamore moved to the sea, and of servants who call themselves unworthy

17.heading: Ten cleansed; one Samaritan returns in thanks
17.note: Ten lepers cry 'have mercy on us'; they are cleansed as they go to the priests; one, a Samaritan, returns to thank him

17.heading: Kingdom not observed as ‘here’ or ‘there’
17.note: Pharisees ask when God's Kingdom comes; he says it comes without observation, no one will say 'Look, here', and it is 'within you'.

17.heading: Suffering first, then sudden Son of Man disclosure
17.note: The Son of Man will shine like lightning across the sky, but first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation

17.heading: Noah, Lot, lost attachment, one taken and one left
17.note: As in Noah's and Lot's days, people ate and drank until flood and fire came; two in one bed, one taken, one left

18.heading: Persistent widow and unjust judge
18.note: A judge who fears neither God nor man defends a widow who keeps coming; God, says Jesus, will quickly avenge his chosen

18.heading: Pharisee and tax collector at prayer
18.note: A Pharisee thanks God he is not like others; a tax collector beats his chest and says 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner'.

18.heading: Infants received and kingdom reception
18.note: People bring babies for him to touch; the disciples rebuke them, but Jesus says 'Allow the little children to come'.

18.heading: Rich ruler, possessions, impossibility, and reward
18.note: Told to sell all, a rich ruler grows sad; a camel through a needle's eye, Jesus says, is easier than a rich man entering

18.heading: Third Jerusalem passion prediction misunderstood
18.note: He tells the twelve the Son of Man will be mocked, scourged and killed, and rise on the third day; they understand none

18.heading: Blind beggar cries out, sees, follows, and sparks praise
18.note: A blind man near Jericho cries 'have mercy on me' and, rebuked, shouts louder; Jesus gives him sight, and he follows glorifying God

19.heading: Zacchaeus seen, hosted, and restored as Abraham's son
19.note: A chief tax collector climbs a sycamore; Jesus says he must stay at his house, and Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor

19.heading: Mina parable: delayed rule, entrusted work, and severe judgment
19.note: A nobleman returns as king; two servants gained minas and are put over cities; one hid his mina and loses it

19.heading: Ascent, colt, and royal acclamation
19.note: Disciples bring a colt, saying 'The Lord needs it'; cloaks line the road; Pharisees object, and he says the stones would cry out

19.heading: Jesus weeps over missed peace and coming siege
19.note: Near the city, he weeps, saying the things for its peace are hidden; enemies will build a barricade and leave no stone on another

19.heading: Temple action, daily teaching, and leaders' plot
19.note: He drives sellers from the temple, calling it a 'den of robbers'; leaders seek to destroy him, but the people hang on his words

20.heading: Authority challenged and John's baptism returned as a question
20.note: Challenged on his authority, he asks if John's baptism was from heaven or men; they say they don't know, so he won't say

20.heading: Tenants, beloved son, rejected stone, and threatened stewards
20.note: Farmers mistreat three servants and kill the owner's beloved son; the vineyard will go to others, and chief priests want to seize Jesus

20.heading: Caesar's denarius and God's claim
20.note: Asked about taxes to Caesar, he asks whose image is on a denarius and says give Caesar's things to Caesar, God's to God

20.heading: Sadducees, seven husbands, and resurrection life
20.note: Sadducees ask whose wife a seven-times married woman will be; he says the raised are like angels, and God is God of the living

20.heading: David's son and David's Lord
20.note: He asks how the Christ is David's son when David in a psalm calls him Lord, saying 'Sit at my right hand'.

20.heading: Scribal display and widows' houses
20.note: He warns disciples of scribes who like long robes and best seats, devour widows' houses, and make long prayers; they will receive greater condemnation

21.heading: A poor widow's whole livelihood
21.note: A poor widow casts two coins into the treasury; he says she put in more than all, giving all she had to live on

21.heading: Temple destruction and warnings against panic
21.note: He says the temple's stones will be thrown down; asked when, he warns of many saying 'I am he', and of wars and earthquakes

21.heading: Persecution, testimony, and endurance
21.note: They will be persecuted and handed over, even by relatives; he will give a mouth and wisdom, and not a hair will perish

21.heading: Jerusalem surrounded, flight, and Gentile times
21.note: When armies surround Jerusalem, those in Judea are told to flee to the mountains; people are led captive and Jerusalem is trampled by Gentiles

21.heading: Cosmic distress, Son of Man, and near redemption
21.note: Signs in sun, moon and stars make men faint; they see the Son of Man coming in a cloud, and are told 'look up'.

21.heading: Fig tree, enduring words, watchfulness, and prayer
21.note: A budding fig tree shows summer is near; so the Kingdom is near; heaven and earth pass away, but his words will not

22.heading: Plot, Passover preparation, bread, and cups
22.note: Judas agrees to deliver him for money; at the Passover he says of the bread 'my body', and of the cup 'the new covenant'.

22.heading: Greatness overturned by the serving Jesus
22.note: A dispute arises over who is greatest; kings lord it over others, he says, but he is among them as one who serves

22.heading: Sifting, Peter's return, and predicted denial
22.note: Jesus says he prayed for Simon against Satan's sifting; Peter says he is ready for prison and death, but will deny him three times

22.heading: Purse, bag, swords, and numbered-with-transgressors fulfillment
22.note: Sent before without purse or bag, they lacked nothing; now he says buy a sword; told of two swords, he says 'That is enough'.

22.heading: Prayer, cup, agony, sleeping disciples, and arrest
22.note: He prays 'not my will, but yours', finds the disciples sleeping, and is met by Judas's crowd; he heals a servant's cut-off ear

22.heading: Peter's denial, Jesus's look, and bitter weeping
22.note: By the fire Peter denies him three times; the rooster crows, the Lord turns and looks at Peter, who goes out and weeps bitterly

22.heading: Mockery and the council's interrogation
22.note: Men mock and beat him, blindfolded; the council asks if he is the Son of God, and he answers 'You say it'.

23.heading: Political charges before Pilate and mockery before Herod
23.note: Accused before Pilate, Jesus answers 'So you say'; Pilate finds no basis and sends him to Herod, who mocks him after getting no answers

23.heading: Repeated innocence verdicts, Barabbas, and Pilate's capitulation
23.note: Pilate finds nothing worthy of death, but the crowd shouts 'Crucify! Crucify him!' and asks for Barabbas; Pilate hands Jesus over

23.heading: Simon, mourning women, and warning for Jerusalem
23.note: Simon of Cyrene is made to carry the cross; Jesus tells the mourning women to weep for themselves and their children, not for him

23.heading: Crucifixion, forgiveness, mockery, and two criminals
23.note: He says 'Father, forgive them' as he is crucified between two criminals; one insults him, the other asks 'remember me' and hears of Paradise

23.heading: Darkness, torn veil, death, and witnesses
23.note: Darkness and a torn temple veil; Jesus cries 'I commit my spirit' and breathes his last; the centurion calls him a righteous man

23.heading: Joseph's tomb and the women's Sabbath preparation
23.note: Joseph, a council member, asks Pilate for the body and lays it in a rock tomb; the women see it, then prepare spices

24.heading: Women at the empty tomb remember and report
24.note: Women find the stone rolled away; two men in dazzling clothing say 'He isn't here, but is risen'; Peter runs and sees the linen

24.heading: Unrecognized Jesus walks and interprets Scripture
24.note: Two on the road to Emmaus, talking of what happened, do not recognize Jesus; he explains from Moses and the prophets what concerns himself

24.heading: Hospitality, broken bread, recognition, and return
24.note: He breaks the bread, their eyes are opened, he vanishes; they return to Jerusalem and hear 'The Lord is risen indeed'.

24.heading: Peace, wounds, touch, and food before the gathered followers
24.note: Jesus stands among them saying 'Peace be to you'; they think they see a spirit; he shows his hands and feet and eats fish

24.heading: Opened minds, worldwide witness, and promised power
24.note: He opens their minds: the Christ must suffer and rise, repentance is preached to all nations, and they wait in Jerusalem for power

24.heading: Blessing, departure, joy, and temple praise
24.note: He lifts his hands, blesses them, and is carried into heaven; they worship him, return with great joy, and praise God in the temple
